title: Petra and the Veil
premise: Lior Thackeray keeps a sealed gate beneath her charm shop, the last door into Vessany, a country erased from maps and memory by a bargain her grandmother struck. When a mute child arrives speaking Old Vessani, Lior learns the erasure is failing — and that the child is the country's living heir, hunted by the Wardens who enforce the Veil. To save the girl, Lior must reopen the gate and lead a ragged remnant of exiles home before the moon's thirteenth turn seals every threshold forever. She succeeds at terrible cost: the Veil falls, Vessany returns to the world, but Lior, half-tied to both sides of the gate, must choose which country she belongs to — and she chooses the one being born, not the one that was lost.
about_author: Yara Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore before turning to fiction. She writes about doors, debts, and the countries people carry inside them.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Knocked at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On an ordinary market night in outlawed-magic Corvane, a barefoot girl appears at Lior's shop speaking a language Lior shouldn't understand but does. The girl's touch makes a dead charm bloom. Emotional beat: dread mixed with recognition — Lior realizes the Veil around her own past is thinning.

chapters.title: Charms for a City That Forbids Them
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Hiding the girl, Neth, among her stock, Lior traces the language to her grandmother's locked ledger and learns Neth bears the seal of Vessany's royal house. A Warden inspector visits the shop on a routine sweep. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve as Lior chooses to lie for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Refused to Say
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with a flashback chapter from her grandmother Sable's journal interleaved. The ledger reveals the Veil was bought with Sable's own name — she traded Vessany's existence to spare it annihilation. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal; inheritance revealed as a debt rather than a gift.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Warden Captain Ilsa Vey's POV. Ilsa investigates the charm shop, haunted by fragments of a homeland she was made to forget. She finds a Vessani coin in Lior's till and lets it go — barely. Emotional beat: loyalty to the Veil cracking against a homesickness she cannot name.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. An exile cartographer confirms the deadline: when the moon completes its thirteenth turn, all thresholds close permanently and Neth dies with them. Lior begins gathering the scattered Vessani remnant. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership; belonging offered by strangers she never expected to claim.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Neth's POV, rendered through Lior's translation. In the smugglers' night-market, the group bargains for passage, paying with memories of Vessany — each payment visibly hollows the seller. Lior pays a memory of her mother. Emotional beat: the cost of truth versus the comfort of forgetting.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ordered to arrest the shopkeeper, Isla instead finds the hidden gate and stands before it weeping at words she can't read. She burns her orders but cannot yet join the exiles. Emotional beat: loyalty split down the middle; truth winning by a thread.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the Shop
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening the gate requires a keeper's blood and a heir's voice together; the attempt tears the Veil early, flooding Corvane with returned magic and drawing every Warden in the city. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration — there is no way back to the small safe life.

chapters.title: The Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Ilsa POVs. Climax: leading exiles and a defected Warden through the collapsing threshold while Wardens close in, Lior confronts Sable's ghost-bound guardian at the gate's heart and answers the original bargain with one of her own. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into authorship — Lior rewrites the terms.

chapters.title: A Door Out, A Door Open
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue-like. The Veil falls; Vessany returns to the world whole, with Neth crowned and Ilsa choosing exile-side citizenship. Lior, bound half to each side, becomes the first ambassador of two countries learning to share a border. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging — not going home, but building one.
